nodes.name: In situ encapsulation and pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: During the crystallization of ZIF-8 (average size d = 50 nm), ruthenium acetylacetonate (Ru(acac)3) and chromium nitrate nonahydrate (Cr(NO3)3·9H2O) were added, and silica (SiO2) was used as a template to increase the surface area of the formed ZIF-8. The sample was pyrolyzed at 950 °C in an Ar atmosphere to evaporate Zn, followed by the removal of SiO2 in a NaOH solution. After the second calcination, the catalysts were obtained.

nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS analysis show that Ru 3p spectra of RuNPs -RuCrAPs -N - C (Figure S11b, Supporting Information) shift to lower binding energy compared to RuNPs -RuSAs -N - C , indicating the lowered oxidation states of Ru

nodes.characterization_summary: The ECSA was measured via the copper underpotential deposition method as 205.07 m2/g.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ECSA of RuNPs-RuCrAPs-N-C is calculated to be 205.07 m2·g-1 , implying its abundant active sites ... based on copper (Cu) underpotential deposition (Cu-UPD) method

nodes.characterization_summary: Tafel analysis shows the RuNPS-RuCrAPs-N-C catalyst has a Tafel slope of 53 mV/dec, suggesting a Volmer-Heyrovsky mechanism.
nodes.evidence_snippet: RuNPs·RuCrAPs·N-C has the lowest Tafel slope of 53 mV·dec-1 ... suggesting that the HER follows the Volmer-Heyrovsky mechanism where the water adsorption and dissociation are rate determining steps

nodes.characterization_summary: Poisoning experiments with EDTA and KSCN demonstrate that Ru nanoparticles are the primary active sites for the HER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDTA can inhibit the activity of Ru SAs while KSCN has the capability to deactivate all Ru species ... observation reveals that the Ru NPs are the main active sites for the HER
